# A merge with a conflict on s and a change only THEY made to t. `sesam status`
# sends the user to resolve s and seal. That seal must not touch t: its
# plaintext is still ours, its object already theirs, and sealing it would
# quietly undo their change for that secret.

sesam-repo admin base.txt ours.txt theirs.txt changed.txt resolved.txt

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
cp $TMPDIR/base.txt t
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec sesam add t --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secrets'

exec git checkout -b topic
cp $TMPDIR/theirs.txt s
cp $TMPDIR/changed.txt t
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change s and t'

exec git checkout master
cp $TMPDIR/ours.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'master: change s'

! exec git merge topic
stderr 'automatically merging revealed file s; 1 conflict'

# Status tells the two apart: s needs a hand, t just lags behind its object.
exec sesam status
stdout 'U s'
stdout 'S t'
stdout 'the stale \(S\) secrets take the incoming version when you finish'

# Resolve s and seal, as the hint says. t is left alone and named.
cp $TMPDIR/resolved.txt s
exec sesam seal
stderr 'not sealed - the object is newer than the plaintext'
stderr 'sesam:   t'
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'RESOLVED'
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/t.sesam
stdout 'CHANGED'

# The finalize refreshes t and both changes survive the merge.
exec git add -A
exec git commit --no-edit
exec cat t
stdout 'CHANGED'
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/t.sesam
stdout 'CHANGED'
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'RESOLVED'
exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'

-- base.txt --
line one
BASE
line three
-- ours.txt --
line one
OURS
line three
-- theirs.txt --
line one
THEIRS
line three
-- changed.txt --
line one
CHANGED
line three
-- resolved.txt --
line one
RESOLVED
line three
